Your task is to reconstruct a tabletop robotic-manipulation workspace from staged assets.

rows.title: Game Port Reference Capture: Magic Tower
rows.summary: Stand-in for the asset-capture step of a Flash-to-modern-engine port: drive the legacy Magic Tower (mota-24) build under Ruffle and collect per-floor reference screenshots that downstream engineers will use as ground-truth for tile layout, HUD placement, and level-script reconstruction.
rows.task_prompt:
## Context

A small game studio plans to re-implement the legacy Flash dungeon-crawler **Magic Tower (mota-24)** on a modern stack. Before any port code is written, the porting workflow requires a clean set of **per-floor reference screenshots** captured from the original build — these screenshots become the visual contract that downstream engineers diff against while re-creating tile maps, HUD elements, and per-floor enemy/item placement.

Your role in that workflow is the reference-capture pass: drive the original game far enough to expose floors 1–3, and save one labeled screenshot per floor reached.

## Goal

Launch the original Flash build under Ruffle, advance through the early-game progression, and produce labeled per-floor reference screenshots up to and including floor 3.

## Steps

1. The game is auto-opened by the task setup at `mota_24_ez\input\mota-24.swf` in Ruffle. If the window is not already focused, focus it. If the local Ruffle software won't open the file properly, load it instead via the web demo at https://ruffle.rs/demo/ (upload the .swf there).
2. Wait for the title / loading screens to finish and enter the running game world.
3. Play forward through floors 1 → 3 using standard movement and interaction (no cheats, no save-state hacks). Combat / item pickups / stair-use are expected; this is what a porting engineer would do to surface each floor.
4. Each time you arrive on a new floor, capture a full-window screenshot of the rendered game and save it to `mota_24_ez\output\$FLOOR_NUMBER$.png`, where `$FLOOR_NUMBER$` is the integer floor index (`1.png`, `2.png`, `3.png`).

## Acceptance

- One PNG per floor reached, named by floor number, exists in the output directory.
- Each PNG must depict the correct floor (visually matches the original game's floor layout) — these will be diffed against held-out reference frames.
agent_must_do: Focus the Ruffle window with mota-24.swf loaded (the task setup auto-launches it)
Wait for the title / loading screens and enter the actual game world
Play forward through floors 1 → 3 using normal movement and interaction (no cheats)
On arrival at each new floor, save a full-window screenshot as output/<floor>.png (1.png, 2.png, 3.png)

input_files.name: mota-24.swf
input_files.description: Flash game to play

rows.title: butterfly_flap_animation
rows.summary: Animate a supplied butterfly image in Adobe After Effects with four wing-flap cycles and a smooth curved 2.5D flight path.
rows.task_prompt:
Create a butterfly wing-flap animation in Adobe After Effects.

Remote workspace:
- Task folder: base

Software:
- Launch Adobe After Effects using: base\software\launch_after_effects.bat
- The installed After Effects version may differ from the original submission; use the available AE version opened by this launcher.
- After Effects is the intended tool, but if AE is not available in the environment, any other way to achieve the goal is welcome (the output MP4 is what gets evaluated).

Visible inputs:
- Source butterfly artwork: base\input\butterfly.jpeg
- Detailed task spec: base\input\task_spec.md

What to do:
1. Import the butterfly image into After Effects.
2. Split or mask the butterfly into a central body plus left and right wings.
3. Set wing anchor points near the wing-body joints.
4. Animate the wings with repeated Y-rotation or equivalent perspective deformation.
5. Produce exactly 4 complete wing flap cycles: open -> closed -> open.
6. Move the butterfly along a smooth curved 2.5D-style path through the frame with at least 2 Y-direction turning points.
7. Keep the butterfly texture recognizably tied to the source image at fully open moments.
8. Use a plain dark or black background so the butterfly motion remains clear.

Export requirements:
- Export one H.264 MP4.
- Frame rate: 30 fps.
- Duration: 4.0 to 5.5 seconds.
- Save the final render exactly here: base\output\output.mp4

Do not modify files under input/. Write only the final MP4 under output/.
agent_must_do: Launch Adobe After Effects from `software/launch_after_effects.bat` (intended tool); if AE is unavailable in the environment, any other approach that produces the required output is acceptable.
Import `input/butterfly.jpeg` and use it as the source butterfly artwork.
Split or mask the butterfly into a central body plus left and right wings.
Animate the wings with repeated Y-rotation or equivalent perspective deformation for exactly 4 complete flap cycles.
Move the butterfly along a smooth curved 2.5D-style path with at least 2 Y-direction turning points.
Use a plain dark or black background for clear motion detection.
Export one 30 fps H.264 MP4, 4.0 to 5.5 seconds long, to `output/output.mp4`.

input_files.name: Butterfly artwork
input_files.description: Agent-visible source artwork to animate

input_files.name: Task specification
input_files.description: Public animation and export requirements

rows.task_prompt:
Goal: Isolate the correct foreground subject from the existing scene in the source clip, create a new Resolve project yourself, place that subject over a uniform bright-green background as indicated by the first-frame target screenshot, and export the finished green-screen plate.

Remote workspace:
- Task folder: crane_flyingsky

Software:
- Launch DaVinci Resolve using: crane_flyingsky\software\DaVinci Resolve.lnk
- No starter `.drp` project is packaged with this task. Create a new Resolve project yourself for the task run.

Inputs (already on remote desktop):
- Input assets live under: crane_flyingsky\input
- Source composite containing the subject in an existing scene: crane_flyingsky\input\input.mp4
- First-frame target screenshot showing the intended subject-on-green result: crane_flyingsky\input\input.png
